title: From Every Fear and Doubt, O Lord
description: From Every Fear and Doubt, O Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 35, “Drawing Near to God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: From ev-ery fear and doubt, O Lord, In mer-cy set us free, While in the con-fi-dence of prayer Our hearts draw near to Thee!

lines: From every fear and doubt, O Lord,
While in the confidence of prayer
Our hearts draw near to Thee!
In all our trials, struggles, joys,
Teach us Thy love to see,
Which by the discipline of life
Our lives, devoted to Thy will,
And then will death, whene'er it come,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
